review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Classical motion and geometric paths; physical scalar/vector quantities; inertia, momentum, force impulse, angular momentum, torque and moment of inertia; kinetic energy and work; transitive moving and rolling actions.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. OpenStax University Physics Volume 1, NPTEL and Russian dictionary sources support technical and lexical corrections. Source prose and exercises are not copied. Qualified labels, intersections and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All additions use U1 with unspecified strength; old home contexts and reviewed genera remain. Physical quantities, motion processes, geometric paths and actions causing movement are separate categories.

sense_decisions.scope: A physical quantity specified by a signed numerical value and a unit, without a spatial direction; the physical restriction is distinct from the U3 Scalar record.
A physical quantity represented by a spatial vector in the selected mechanics model, not a disease carrier or a programming container.
Resistance to changes of velocity, applicable to resting and moving bodies. The inertial-frame law concerns net external force, not the absence of every individual force.
The classical mass-times-velocity quantity relative to a frame; distinct from force impulse and metaphorical impetus.
The time integral of a force over an interval, not the force itself and not momentum at a single instant.
The impulse of the net external force over the chosen interval; the change in linear momentum is a theorem relating quantities, not a synonym for momentum.
Angular momentum with respect to a chosen origin; a distinct quantity from linear momentum, including for a particle on a straight path.
The moment of a force about a chosen origin; an axial vector quantity in classical mechanics, not simply a kind of force.
The scalar mass-distribution quantity for a specified axis; distinguish it from inertia as a general property, area moments and the full inertia tensor.
The geometric path traced by a moving point in a selected frame; distinguish the path from its length, the motion process and a displacement vector.
A trajectory contained in a plane.
A trajectory forming a closed path; no periodic timing or constant speed is implied.
The intersection of planar and closed trajectories.
The accumulated path length over a motion interval, including retraced portions; it is not generally the magnitude of the net displacement.
Motion of a rigid body with unchanged orientation in the chosen frame; all body points have the same instantaneous velocity, but it need not be constant over time.
Motion along a curved path, without requiring a rigid body to change orientation.
Pure translation along straight paths.
Pure translation along congruent curved paths; the rigid-body orientation stays unchanged.
The intersection of straight pure translation and constant speed.
Rigid-body rotation about an axis fixed in the selected frame; no constant angular speed is required.
Motion combining rotation of the body and progression over a surface; distinguish it from pushing an object so that it rolls.
Rolling with no relative sliding velocity at the instantaneous contact with the surface.
Rolling accompanied by sliding at the contact surface.
Energy associated with motion relative to the chosen frame; no universal nonzero value is assigned.
The kinetic energy associated with translation of the body center of mass in the selected classical frame.
The kinetic-energy contribution of rotation about the specified axis in the rigid-body model.
The signed scalar quantity for energy transfer by a force along a displacement; distinguish it from employment and from torque.
Determining the classical linear momentum vector in a specified frame.
Determining force impulse over a specified interval.
Determining angular momentum about the selected origin.
Determining torque relative to a specified origin or axis.
Determining a mass moment of inertia for the specified axis.
Determining accumulated travel distance rather than net displacement.
The kinetic-energy restriction of the existing energy-measurement action.
Determining the work quantity for a specified physical process.
The U3 Scalar record remains unchanged; it is not silently equated with a physical scalar quantity.
The broad path record remains untouched; the new trajectory is specifically the geometric motion path.
The time-point moment is not a moment of force, moment of inertia or angular momentum.
Employment work remains separate from the physical work quantity.
Riding and recreational skating remain separate from mechanical rolling and transitive rolling actions.
The inherited 80-percent motion-to-sound assertion is outside this batch and remains queued, not newly endorsed.
Do not import the dictionary angular-momentum-under-linear-momentum genus.
Do not import torque as a force subtype or identify it with mechanical work.
Use the quantitative mass-distribution meaning, not a synonym for qualitative inertia.

review.limits: The quantitative meanings use classical mechanics with specified frames, origins or axes. No universal constant-speed translation, scalar/vector identification, angular-under-linear momentum, torque-under-force, inertia-as-rest, full inertia tensor or new numerical law is encoded. Component motions of rolling are not treated as pure-translation genera. General reference-frame models, collisions, units for new quantities, potential energy, motion-to-sound probabilities and wider generated motion aliases remain queued.

exclusion_review.decision: Preserve clear scans and all upper exclusions and explicit negations. No new disjointness assertion is needed for the reviewed distinctions.

review.collision_decision: No new normalized-term collisions accepted. Reuse existing movement, rotation, quantity and transitive-action records; qualify the new meanings away from computer Scalar, work and time-point moment.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
